By Tim Brown | The Oregonian/OregonLive The 2026 NCAA men’s college basketball tournament really gets underway with the first round of the March Madness taking place today. 16 games tip off on Wednesday, and another 16 on Friday. Who will move on from the Round of 64 field and into Round 2? Our complete streaming guide has start times and TV details for every matchup. Watch games streaming free What is the schedule of games for the 2026 NCAA Tournament? Here are the most important dates for the rest of the 2026 NCAA men’s basketball tournament: Second Round : Saturday, March 21 and Sunday, March 22 Sweet 16 : Thursday, March 26 and Friday, March 27 Elite Eight : Saturday, March 28 and Sunday, March 29 Final Four : 6 p.m. and 8:30 p.m. ET on Saturday, April 4 on TBS at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis NCAA championship game : 8:30 p.m. ET on Monday, April 6 on TBS at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis How can I watch March Madness basketball games streaming free? If you don’t have cable and just want the cheapest possible way to watch all of March Madness this year, here’s a look at the best ways to watch all of the NCAA Tournament over the next couple of weeks. The quickest and easiest way to watch this week’s games live for free is with DIRECTV (free trial). The second best option: Sling is the cheapest way to watch every NCAA tournament game (costs under $25 for the first month) except those being broadcast on CBS. However, if your TV doesn’t already have one built in, you can get a HDTV antenna to pair with your Sling subscription in order to get the games being broadcast on your local CBS station as well. If you don’t have time to order a HDTV antenna, another way to see all games broadcast on CBS is by signing up for Paramount+ on a free trial . This way you will be able to watch every game broadcast on CBS up through the Elite Eight. Paramount+ costs just $12.99/month after the free trial ends and you can use it to watch on your smart TV, phone, or tablet. If you already have cable, use your login information to watch every NCAA Tournament game live through the March Madness Live app when you sign in with your cable provider login information. This way you can watch on your phone when you’re out and about.
